title: Mary Gay Scanlon criticizes GOP health care negotiations and pipeline bill - South Delco News
text:
Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon, who represents Pennsylvania’s 5th district in the U.S. House of Representatives, used her social media platform on December 12, 2025 to comment on ongoing debates over healthcare policy and energy legislation in Congress.
In a post made at 15:06 UTC, Scanlon criticized House Republican leadership for their approach to developing a healthcare plan, stating: “The fact that @SpeakerJohnson has to negotiate with the ‘five families’ to come up with the concepts of a healthcare plan tells everything you need to know about @HouseGOP. They’re negotiating how to divide up the spoils, not what’s best for the American people.”
Later that day at 18:17 UTC, she addressed impending changes in healthcare coverage due to congressional action or inaction: “We have until December 19th, before 15 million Americans will lose their healthcare coverage. The Senate blocked an extension of the ACA tax credits, and @HouseGOP only has ‘concepts of a plan.’ @HouseDemocrats have a discharge petition to extend the tax credits and save”
At 18:18 UTC on December 12, Scanlon commented on recent energy legislation votes: “Once again, Republican leadership in DC has decided that maximizing profits for the oil and gas industry is more important than the health and safety of the American people. I voted against the Unsafe Pipelines Review Act because Pennsylvanians deserve the opportunity to weigh”
Mary Gay Scanlon has represented Pennsylvania’s 5th District since winning her seat in Congress in 2018. She succeeded Pat Meehan after his resignation. Born in Watertown, New York in 1959 and currently residing in Swarthmore, Scanlon is an alumna of Colgate University (BA) and earned her JD from the University of Pennsylvania.
Scanlon’s recent statements reflect ongoing partisan disputes over healthcare policy—specifically related to ACA tax credits—and concerns about legislative priorities regarding energy infrastructure.
